# Screen & Tab Layout

How to arrange components correctly and well on a `b1_screen` — panels, page content, resizable split panes, and tabs. Produces a valid structure on the first try and follows enterprise-app best practice, so you do not build something that saves but looks wrong. For the layout *inside* a form, see the Form Layout skill.

---

## Trigger Phrases

Use this skill whenever a request touches where things go or how the screen is divided:

- add a chart / map / grid / form to the screen; put X next to or below Y
- split into tabs; use tabs; one at a time; too cramped; small monitor
- side by side; stacked; two columns; three columns; dashboard
- resizable; draggable divider; splitter; split panes
- rearrange; move X to its own area
- any time you add a SECOND visual component to a screen or a panel

---

## The one mental model (everything below follows from this)

> **B1-931:** the old `layout` attribute (fixed codes `1C`/`2E`/`2U`/`3E`/`3W`/`3T`) and `layoutPosition` are **removed**. No object type carries them any more — never set either. Any older guidance that says "set `layout` on the screen" or "position the panel with `layoutPosition`" no longer applies.

There are exactly **two** ways to arrange a screen:

1. **Page content (the default — most screens).** The screen renders its top-level `b1_panel` cards in document order; the arrangement is a Tailwind grid/flex you put in the **screen `htmlClass`**. No splitter bars. Covers dashboards, columns, stacked sections, master-detail — see Level 1.
2. **Split panes (opt-in, resizable).** Only when the user should be able to **drag a divider** to resize regions, add a **`b1_splitpanes`** whose children are **`b1_pane`** instances — see Level 2.

The shape, nested:

```
SCREEN / FRAME / DIALOG / TAB      (page content; its htmlClass IS the layout)
  PANEL per card  (b1_panel, shared master 31572117-2fe3-4262-ba03-20a74c6b59ca)
    content, ONE of:
      - a widget   (grid, chart, map, form, card_view, tree_grid ...)
      - a TABBAR (b1_tabbar) -> TABS (b1_tab); each tab is page content again (recurses)
  OR, for a resizable region:
  b1_splitpanes (direction) -> b1_pane (two or more) -> b1_panel -> widget
```

Verified type facts — do not assume otherwise:

- There is **no `layout` attribute and no `layoutPosition`** — not on screens, frames, dialogs, tabs or panels. Setting them fails validation as an unknown attribute.
- `b1_screen`, `b1_frame`, `b1_dialog` and `b1_tab` are all page content by default. A tab is a mini-screen: it has its own `htmlClass` and its own panels.
- Panels render in **document order**; the visual arrangement comes entirely from the owner's `htmlClass`. Name top-level panels `a`, `b`, `c`, … for a stable reading order.
- `b1_form` is a `b1_panel` subtype and may sit directly on page content like a panel. `b1_tabbar` also subtypes `b1_panel`, but only so a panel accepts it as a child — a tabbar is NOT a panel itself and always sits INSIDE its own panel card, never directly on a screen/frame/dialog/tab (validation rejects it).
- Non-visual instances (`b1_data_source`) stay at the **screen root** — never inside panes or panels. A content object's own toolbar sits in that content's panel; a screen-wide toolbar is a screen-level instance (see the sticky-toolbar note in Level 1).

---

## Level 1 — Page content (the default)

The cards are the screen's **top-level panels** (one per card); the layout class lives on the **screen `htmlClass`**. Full reference: `blueprint_dsl/page-content-screens.md`.

Rules (enforced or strongly idiomatic):

1. ONE visual component per panel. N components means N card panels. Adding a widget means adding a panel — NOT dropping it into an existing panel.
2. Put the layout class on the **screen `htmlClass`**, prefixed with `p-6 overflow-auto` for a padded, scrolling page — e.g. `p-6 overflow-auto grid grid-cols-3 gap-4 auto-rows-fr`, or `p-6 overflow-auto flex flex-col gap-4`. Page content applies **no default padding/gap** — include them yourself.
3. The card header comes from `headerLabel` on the panel or on its content object. Per-card spanning/sizing goes on that **panel's own `htmlClass`** (e.g. `col-span-2`).
4. No wrapper panel at the top level — the screen `htmlClass` *is* the layout box.

Common recipes (set on the screen `htmlClass`, always with `p-6 overflow-auto`):

| Goal | Screen `htmlClass` |
|---|---|
| 2 / 3 / 4 columns of cards | `grid grid-cols-N gap-4 auto-rows-fr` (N = 2, 3 or 4) |
| 2x2 grid | `grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 auto-rows-fr` |
| Stacked, equal height | `grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 auto-rows-fr` |
| Stacked, natural height | `flex flex-col gap-4` |
| Sidebar + main | `grid grid-cols-3 gap-4` + `col-span-2` on the main panel |
| Responsive (1 then 2 then 4) | `grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4 auto-rows-max lg:auto-rows-fr` |

Gotchas:

- **Only safelisted layout/spacing/sizing utilities render in `htmlClass`** (display, flex, grid, gap, align, padding/margin, sizing, overflow, plus the `sm:`/`md:`/`lg:` min-width prefixes). Colours, borders, radius, shadows and typography are NOT safelisted and do nothing — the exception is the themed `b1-glass-*` frosted-background classes, which are real component-library classes.
- **Cards stretch by default.** To make a card fit its content use the important variants `h-fit! grow-0! shrink-0` (a plain `h-fit`/`grow-0` loses to an unlayered framework rule). For equal-height cards use a grid with `auto-rows-fr` — desktop-only (`lg:auto-rows-fr`) on responsive screens.
- **Several cards in one cell:** make the cell panel a chrome-less container with `panelType: "structural"` plus an `htmlClass`, then nest one card panel per card inside it.
- **Sticky toolbar:** add a toolbar as a screen-level instance (sibling of the panels) with `htmlClass: "grouped mx-6 mt-6 w-auto!"` — the `w-auto!` is required because the toolbar hard-codes `width: 100%`.

Copy a working sample (Samples module): `SampleLayoutCols2` (master-detail), `SampleLayoutCols3`, `SampleLayoutCols4`, `SampleLayoutGrid2x2`, `SampleLayoutStack3`, `SampleLayoutResponsive`, `SampleLayoutSidebar`, `SampleLayoutSingle` (single panel).

---

## Level 2 — Split panes (resizable regions)

Only when the user should **drag a divider** — a master grid next to a detail form, a chat beside a preview. Full reference: `blueprint_dsl/layouts-in-screens.md`.

- **`b1_splitpanes`** — the resizable container. `direction: "horizontal"` = panes side by side; `direction: "vertical"` = panes stacked. Children **must** be **two or more** `b1_pane` instances (a single pane is pointless — put the content directly on the screen).
- **`b1_pane`** — one resizable slot, pure geometry: `size`, `minSize`, `maxSize` (percentages 0–100, empty = equal share / no limit). Give each pane a stable, meaningful `instanceName` — per-user resize is persisted by that name.
- Inside each pane put **one `b1_panel`** wrapping the actual widget. Nest a `b1_splitpanes` inside a pane for complex geometries — nesting is unlimited, so any shape is expressible.
- Shared masters to instantiate: **`SimpleB1Splitpanes`**, **`SimpleB1Pane`**, **`SimpleB1Panel`** (reference by name — the MCP tools resolve GUIDs).

Classic shapes:

- Master-detail side by side → horizontal splitpanes, two panes (grid, form).
- Stacked resizable sections → vertical splitpanes.
- Banner on top, two work zones below → vertical splitpanes; the second pane holds a horizontal splitpanes.
- One resizable boundary inside a grid screen → wrap those cells in a `panelType: "structural"` panel carrying the grid-span classes, and put the splitpanes inside it (see `SampleLayoutResponsive`).

Per-shape samples (Samples module): `SampleLayoutSplit2U` / `2E` (two panes), `SampleLayoutSplit3W` / `3E` / `3T` / `3U` / `3L` / `3J` (three panes) — one for each classic shape code. To switch an existing screen between shapes with the SAME pane count (e.g. 2U → 2E), run `node src/cli/scripts/layout/convert-layout.mjs <screenName> <code> [--dry-run]` — it reuses the leaf panes (GUIDs, links and per-user sizes survive), rebuilds only the geometry wrappers, and refuses a pane-count mismatch (a 2-pane screen cannot become `3W`).

Example — master-detail via compose:

```
compose(target: "productsSearch", ops: [
  { op: "add", object: "SimpleB1Splitpanes", as: "split", attrs: { direction: "horizontal" } },
  { op: "add", object: "SimpleB1Pane", into: "split", as: "pane_a" },
  { op: "add", object: "SimpleB1Pane", into: "split", as: "pane_b" },
  { op: "add", object: "SimpleB1Panel", into: "pane_a", as: "a" },
  { op: "add", object: "SimpleB1Panel", into: "pane_b", as: "b" },
  { op: "add", object: "productsGrid", into: "a" },
  { op: "add", object: "productsForm", into: "b" }
])
```

Validation (enforced by the MCP on every mutation): fewer than two panes, a bad `direction`, a `size`/`minSize`/`maxSize` outside 0–100, or a non-`b1_pane` child of a splitpanes are all rejected.

Prefer the templates — `create_from_template('MasterDetailSearch')` already yields a side-by-side splitpanes tree; `MaintenanceScreen` yields a single-panel page-content screen. Refine with `compose` / `set_field`.

---

## Level 3 — Tabs (when one screen has too much)

When components compete for space (too cramped, small monitor, one at a time), move them into a `b1_tabbar` in one panel. ONE component per tab — N components means N tabs. The classic mistake is one combined tab holding everything.

Correct structure — a tabbar in panel `b`, two tabs, each a mini page-content screen:

```
panel b
  Tabbar  (master from search_blueprint(tabbar))
    Tab  label=Map
      Panel  ->  the Map widget
    Tab  label=Recent Revenue
      Panel  ->  the Chart widget
```

Each tab is page content: **wrap every widget in its own `b1_panel`** inside the tab and arrange the panels with the tab's `htmlClass`. A tab does **not** auto-wrap loose children — a widget placed directly in a tab renders but mis-sizes (maps collapse to zero height). For a resizable split inside a tab, add a `b1_splitpanes` with `b1_pane` children, exactly as on a screen. Discover the panel/tabbar/tab masters with search_blueprint (topics: panel, tabbar, tab).

---

## Restructuring an EXISTING screen (wrap into tabs / splitter, move things)

Never rebuild a screen with `mode:"replace"` just to rearrange it — that payload scales with the whole screen and grows every round. Express the change itself in ONE `patch_blueprint` merge call: send only the NEW container(s) and pull the existing widgets in with `{"$ref": "<instanceName>"}` children. A `$ref` MOVES that instance — entire subtree, GUIDs and links intact — to that spot.

Wrap two existing panels (`a` = grid, `b` = map) in a resizable splitter:

```
patch_blueprint(objectName: "MyScreen", preview: true, instances: '[
  { "objectMasterGuid": "SimpleB1Splitpanes", "instanceName": "split",
    "attributes": { "direction": "horizontal" }, "instances": [
      { "objectMasterGuid": "SimpleB1Pane", "instanceName": "pane_a", "instances": [ { "$ref": "a" } ] },
      { "objectMasterGuid": "SimpleB1Pane", "instanceName": "pane_b", "instances": [ { "$ref": "b" } ] }
  ] }
]')
```

Move existing panels into new tabs the same way: add the Tabbar with its Tab children and put `{ "$ref": "<panel>" }` inside each tab. A `$ref` node may carry overrides (`attributes`, children, `objectSequence`) that merge onto the moved instance. For a single move or an attribute tweak, `compose` ops (`move` / `set`) do the same job. Either way the payload is proportional to the CHANGE, not the screen.

---

## Best practice for enterprise business apps (beyond technically valid)

- One primary component per card/pane. Do not crowd two charts or grids into one panel even though it saves — give each its own panel or tab. Clarity beats density.
- Reach for tabs when widgets exceed two or three per screen region, or on small / non-wide monitors. Tabs keep a clean primary view and hide secondary detail until needed. Keep the PRIMARY list/grid always visible in its own panel ABOVE the tabbar (first in sequence) — move only SECONDARY views (map, chart, history) into tabs.
- Master-detail is the workhorse: a list drives a detail form or chart via selection. Resizable → horizontal splitpanes; fixed → page content with `grid grid-cols-2 gap-4`. Use page content unless the user actually needs to drag the boundary.
- Stable reading order: put the primary list / most-important panel first (`a`).
- Do not over-nest. Tabs inside tabs, or deeply nested splitpanes, are rarely warranted — prefer a second screen.
- Responsive intent: if the user mentions a small screen, author mobile-first with the safelisted prefixes (`flex flex-col md:flex-row`, `grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2`) or use tabs.

---

## Common mistakes this skill prevents

- Error "has invalid attributes: layout" (or `layoutPosition`) -> the removed B1-931 attributes were set -> remove them; arrange with the owner's `htmlClass`, or add a `b1_splitpanes` for a resizable region.
- New chart/map shares another widget's panel -> a second content object was added to one panel -> give the new widget its own card panel (and grid cell or pane).
- Tabs produced one combined tab -> one tab held both widgets -> one tab per widget, each widget wrapped in a `b1_panel` inside its tab.
- A splitpanes with a single pane -> rejected by validation -> use two or more panes, or drop the splitpanes and use page content.
- A class in `htmlClass` "does nothing" -> it is not safelisted -> only layout/spacing/sizing utilities (plus `b1-glass-*`) render; extend the safelist in `tailwind.css` for anything else.
- A widget placed loose in a tab collapses to zero height -> not wrapped in a panel -> wrap each tab widget in its own `b1_panel`.

# Query a Data Source

Use the `query_data_source` tool (B1_Blueprint MCP) to run a Data Source Object (DSO) and read back its records — or the error it throws. Use it to verify a DSO works right after you create or edit one, and to diagnose a screen that shows no data. It is read-only (fetch only).

## When to use
- After creating or editing a DSO, confirm it returns data.
- Reproduce what a screen would show by passing the same filters.
- Diagnose an empty screen: if the DSO returns rows here, the problem is the screen wiring; if it errors here, fix the DSO first.

## Parameters
- `dataSourceName` (required): the b1_data_source* object name.
- `limit` (default 1): max records; the default returns just the first record — a cheap does-it-work check.
- `skip` (default 0): pagination offset.
- `orderBy`: e.g. `createdAt desc`; falls back to the DSO defaultOrderBy.
- `filters`: same shape a DSO takes — a bare array of {field, operator, value} (AND-combined) or a full {logic, filters} object with nested groups. Operators: eq, neq, gt, lt, ge, le, contains, begins, ends, isNull.
- `fieldlist` (default *): comma-separated field list.
- `resultFilter`: JMESPath applied to the response, e.g. records[].{id: id, name: name}.

The response includes dataSource, type, appliedQuery, recordCount, and records.

## Supported vs unsupported
Supported: framework, application, server, connector, internal rest, and mockup DSOs.
Unsupported (their fetch runs in the browser session): SCL/OpenEdge and external or templated REST — these return a clear message; verify them from the running app instead.

## Notes
- Read-only: to verify create/update/delete, use the running app.
- Runs as the calling user, so per-user authorization applies (anonymized fields stay anonymized).
- After creating a connector DSO, query it with limit 1 to confirm the provider/object mapping and credentials work before wiring screens.

# Build.One Framework Knowledge

Look up framework knowledge **on demand** with the informational MCP tools — search for what the task needs instead of bulk-reading documentation files.

## B1_Knowledge MCP

### searchBlueprintDocs
Semantic search over the complete Build.One framework documentation (architecture, Blueprint DSL, screens, forms, grids, data sources, client logic, deployment, testing).

- `query` — a focused natural-language question, e.g. "how do I link a grid to a maintenance screen" or "filter form operator mapping"
- `topK` (optional) — number of results
- `sessionId` (optional) — pass the same id across related queries so follow-ups are deduplicated against earlier results
- `category` / `filters` (optional) — narrow to a doc category

Use it for every "how do I … / what is … / which attribute …" question. Ask several small, focused queries rather than one broad one, and refine based on what comes back.

### get_blueprint_database_schema
Returns the blueprint database schema (tables, columns, conventions, standard link-type GUIDs). **Always call it before writing SQL** against the blueprint database.

## B1_Blueprint MCP — discovery tools

For what already exists in the blueprint (instead of how the framework works):

- `search_blueprint` — reuse-ranked search for existing templates, exemplar screens, widgets and parts for a topic
- `get_templates` / `get_object_type_samples` — templates and sample objects for a given object type
- `list_object_types` / `search_object_types` / `get_object_type` — discover object types
- `get_object_type_props` / `validate_props` — valid attributes for a type

## Workflow

1. Question about framework concepts or syntax → `searchBlueprintDocs`.
2. About to write SQL → `get_blueprint_database_schema` first.
3. About to build something → `search_blueprint` / `get_object_type_samples` to find patterns to reuse (only follow objects from the "Samples" / "object_type_samples" modules).

## Key Rules

- **Blueprint**: model-based DSL stored in the database, interpreted by the rendering engine at runtime
- **MCP-first**: ALWAYS use MCP tools to query/update blueprints, NEVER edit blueprint JSON files directly
- **Samples module**: only use objects from "Samples" / "object_type_samples" for patterns and best practices

# Create a demo video

One YAML file is one video. `demos/<demo-id>/demo.yaml` holds the storyboard —
scenes, voice-over, cue markers, browser actions, assertions, branding — and the
pipeline turns it into an MP4, an SRT and a reproducible run manifest:

```text
demo.yaml -> voice-over + cue timestamps -> Playwright scenes
          -> Remotion composition -> MP4 + SRT + run-manifest.json
```

Everything below runs from `src/app-server-ts`. The pipeline lives in its
`demo-factory/` folder (beside `src/`), its dependencies are the app server's
own, and `yarn demo:*` scripts in the app server's `package.json` wrap the CLI
(`node demo-factory/src/cli.mjs`). The root `yarn install` installs everything.

The same four stages are buttons on the **Demo Factory Studio** screen (app
`b1-demo-factory`, `DemoFactoryScreen`). The screen and this skill drive
identical code — the CLI is what you use when authoring, the screen is what a
human uses to re-run a stage.

---

## Phase 1: Decide the story before writing YAML

A scene earns its place by making **one statement** and showing **one visible
proof** of it. From `AUTHORING.md`:

- 15 to 45 seconds
- one statement, one visible piece of evidence
- at most three meaningful interactions
- unambiguous start and end state
- **no dependence on what another scene left behind** — every scene records in a
  fresh browser context

Three to five scenes is a product video. More than that is a training course,
and it will not survive the next UI change.

## Phase 2: Verify the screen exists, and that it has data

This is the step that is skipped and then costs a re-record. Two checks, both
before a line of YAML:

1. **The screen is in this blueprint.** `list_objects` / `get_object` on the
   B1_Blueprint MCP. A demo vendored from another repository routinely names a
   screen that does not exist here — `sales-tour-planning` targets
   `SalesTourPlanningScreen`, which lives in vanguard's Samples module and not
   in this one, so it validates and renders but can never record.
2. **Its data source actually returns rows.** `query_data_source` on the DSO
   behind the view you intend to film. An empty result is a filmed chart with a
   0.0–1.0 axis and no bars, and it is the reason `opportunities-map` films two
   views and not the three that exist.

Also check what the screen *renders* for the fields you narrate. The Amount
column on `OpportunitiesMapScreen` is anonymized to `***********` by the
restricted-events handler and then formatted as `$NaN` — true of the app, fatal
in a video. Narrate around it or fix it, but do not film it.

## Phase 3: Write the storyboard

Create `demos/<demo-id>/demo.yaml`. The id is lowercase, digits and hyphens
(`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`), and it must equal the directory name.

`src/schema.mjs` is the contract — read it rather than guessing. The shape:

```yaml
schemaVersion: 1                 # literal 1
id: my-demo                      # == directory name
title: A sentence, not a label   # this is the video's opening title
description: One paragraph on what the video argues.

settings:
  language: en
  viewport: {width: 1920, height: 1080}
  fps: 30
  baseUrl:
    env: B1_BASE_URL             # the env var that overrides the fallback
    fallback: http://localhost:8080/?app=sample-app
  authStateEnv: B1_AUTH_STATE
  headlessEnv: DEMO_HEADLESS
  holdBeforeMs: 700              # stillness before the first action
  holdAfterMs: 1400              # stillness after the last one
  cursor: {enabled: true, moveDurationMs: 700, clickLeadMs: 120, clickEffectDurationMs: 560, sizePx: 30}
  narration:
    provider: auto               # auto | elevenlabs | silent
    voiceIdEnv: ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID
    apiKeyEnv: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY
    modelIdEnv: ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID
    defaultModelId: eleven_multilingual_v2
    languageCodeEnv: ELEVENLABS_LANGUAGE_CODE
    defaultLanguageCode: en
    wordsPerMinute: 132          # only used to estimate timing when silent
  branding:
    productName: Build.One
    accentColor: "#1266f1"
    backgroundColor: "#0b1020"
    textColor: "#f7f8ff"
    showCaptions: true
    showSceneTitles: true

scenes:
  - id: live-pipeline            # ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$
    title: The pipeline, straight from Salesforce
    route: /screens/OpportunitiesMapScreen   # must start with /
    narration: >
      Spoken text. [cue:show-list] Markers are not spoken — they are timestamps.
    actions: []
    assertions: []
```

The quickest correct start is to copy `demos/opportunities-map/demo.yaml` and
replace the scenes: its `settings` block is the one verified against this
workspace.

### Cue markers are the timing model

`[cue:name]` inside narration marks a moment in the voice-over. ElevenLabs
returns character-level timestamps, so an action bound to `atCue: name` fires
exactly when the voice reaches that word. Without an ElevenLabs key the timing
is estimated from text length and `wordsPerMinute` — same file, silent video.

Every `atCue` **must** name a marker present in that scene's own narration;
validate fails otherwise. Markers are stripped before speech synthesis.

### Actions

`goto`, `click`, `fill`, `press`, `hover`, `highlight`, `waitFor`, `screenshot`.
Bind each to a cue (`atCue`) or an absolute time (`atMs`), optionally nudged by
`offsetMs`.

```yaml
    actions:
      - action: waitFor
        atCue: show-list
        target: {demoId: opportunity-table}
        timeoutMs: 30000
      - action: highlight
        atCue: read-row
        target: {css: '.p-datatable-tbody > tr:nth-child(2)'}
        durationMs: 3200
```

Target selectors, in order of preference:

1. `demoId:` — a `data-demo-id` attribute. Layout and CSS may change; these
   stay. This is the contract the app is supposed to honour.
2. `role:` + `name:`
3. `label:` or `text:`
4. `css:` — last resort, and the first thing to break

The synthetic cursor moves to the target on its own for `click`, `fill`,
`press`, `hover` and `highlight`, starting *before* the cue so the action still
lands on it. Never put screen coordinates in a demo.

### Assertions

Every scene should prove it filmed something. Two forms:

```yaml
    assertions:
      - visible: {css: '.leaflet-marker-icon >> nth=0'}
      - textContains: {target: {css: '.p-datatable'}, value: 'Negotiation/Review'}
```

**Verify every selector against the running app before recording** — open the
screen, confirm the element exists and is what you think it is. A selector
invented from reading Vue source is the single most common cause of a scene
that records a blank page.

## Phase 4: Validate

```bash
cd src/app-server-ts
yarn demo:validate <demo-id>
```

Schema, cue references, ids and actions. Costs nothing; run it after every edit.

## Phase 5: Prepare the voice-over

```bash
yarn demo:prepare <demo-id> [--voice=elevenlabs|silent]
```

Creates a **new run** under `output/<demo-id>/<run-id>/`, synthesizes or
estimates the narration, derives cue and caption timestamps, and writes
`run-manifest.json`. Narration is content-addressed in `.cache/narration/`, so
unchanged text never calls ElevenLabs twice.

Without `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` / `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` this still succeeds: the
video comes out silent and captioned, with timing estimated from text length.
That is a legitimate deliverable, not a failure.

## Phase 6: Record

```bash
yarn demo:record <demo-id> [--scenes=scene-a,scene-b]
```

Records into the **latest** run — so `prepare` first, always. Each scene gets a
fresh browser context and is bound to its cue timestamps.

Three things it needs, and the first two are how it fails:

- **`B1_BASE_URL` must carry the app query.** It overrides the demo's own
  fallback, so `http://localhost:8080` alone records the *default* app and your
  screen never appears. Use `http://localhost:8080/?app=sample-app`.
- **A signed-in session.** `B1_AUTH_STATE` (a Playwright storage state) wins
  where one exists; otherwise `record.mjs` sends `B1_USER_API_KEY` as a context
  header, which authenticates navigation and XHR alike. With neither, the run
  stops rather than film the sign-in page. `yarn demo:auth:workspace` mints a
  state from the API key where the auth server supports the handoff;
  `demo-factory/tools/auth-from-session.mjs` takes a `b1.session_token` cookie from a browser
  you are already signed into.
- **A browser.** Playwright's managed Chromium, or a system one named by
  `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH`.

`--scenes` re-records part of a run, but only one whose previous recording
**completed** — an aborted run has no manifest to reuse.

## Phase 7: Render

```bash
REMOTION_OFFTHREADVIDEO_CACHE_MB=512 REMOTION_CONCURRENCY=2 yarn demo:render <demo-id>
```

Composes clips, voice-over, titles, callouts and captions. On a 16 GB workspace
an uncapped render dies partway with `Compositor exited with signal SIGTERM`, so
keep the cache cap unless you know the host is bigger.

Output lands in `output/<demo-id>/<run-id>/`:

- `<demo-id>.mp4`
- `<demo-id>.srt`
- `run-manifest.json` — the reproducible record of the run

`yarn demo:publish:web <demo-id>` copies a finished run into the web app's
public folder. `yarn demo <demo-id>` is all of it in one process
(validate → auth → prepare → record → render).

Paths in `output/`, `.cache/` and `demos/` are relative to
`src/app-server-ts/demo-factory`.

## When the host cannot record or render

Recording needs a browser and rendering needs ffmpeg and ffprobe. In a
workspace, `.devcontainer/scripts/provision-demo-factory.sh` installs both into
the app server's container on every start (`yarn demo:provision` by hand); the
app server's image ships both. The Studio screen asks the server what it can do and disables the
stages it cannot run, with the reason attached.

If you are on a host without them, **stop at Phase 5 and say so**. A validated,
prepared demo is a complete deliverable: it means the storyboard is correct, the
narration is cached, and a human can press Record and Render in the Studio. Do
not fake a video, and do not report a demo as produced when only its YAML exists.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Invalid demo id` | id has uppercase or underscores | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`, matching the directory |
| validate fails on a cue | `atCue` names a marker not in that scene's narration | markers are per scene, not per demo |
| Records the wrong app | `B1_BASE_URL` without `?app=` | `http://localhost:8080/?app=sample-app` |
| Records the sign-in page | no storage state and no API key | set `B1_USER_API_KEY`, or mint `B1_AUTH_STATE` |
| Scene is blank | selector never matched | verify it in the running app; prefer `data-demo-id` |
| Scene works alone, fails in sequence | it depends on another scene's UI state | every scene starts in a fresh context |
| `Compositor exited with signal SIGTERM` | uncapped render on a small host | `REMOTION_OFFTHREADVIDEO_CACHE_MB=512 REMOTION_CONCURRENCY=2` |
| `record` finds no run | `prepare` not run, or the last run aborted | re-run `prepare` |

## UI construction rules (hard-won — do not skip)

- **Multi-column forms need a `SimpleB1FormColumn` separator.** The renderer splits a container's children into columns ONLY at `b1_form_column` separator instances — two "column" blocks without a separator between them silently render as one vertical column, with no error. Responsive recipe: wrapper block `htmlClass "flex flex-col lg:flex-row gap-4"` → colA block (`"flex-1 min-w-0"`) → `SimpleB1FormColumn` → colB block (`"flex-1 min-w-0"`).
- **Status/priority/state grid columns are option chips, not text.** Use the `OptionColumn` master (`b1_option_column`) with `optionsList`, `optionsListTypes` (`value:severity`, severities `info|warn|success|danger`) and `optionsListIcons` (`value:i-lucide-*`; an icon containing `loader` spins — map running/building states to `i-lucide-loader-circle`). `optionsList*` attributes are NOT valid on plain `b1_column_field` instances.
- **Hidden key columns use `enabled: false`** — `b1_column_field` has no `visible` attribute. The key field must exist as a grid column or `selectedRecord` will not carry it for `repositionTo`.
- **Grid LINK column actions reference `b1_code` GUIDs** (LaunchScreen `8bc198e6-1afb-aebb-da14-48a39869c351`, OpenExternalUrl `f5663e5f-37ea-488d-bdb0-46675cdb7cbd`) — a `b1_action` GUID fails silently.
- **Give every screen role its own DSO object** (search list vs. maintenance detail vs. JOINed child) — DSO state is shared per object master, so reuse across roles couples screens. For JOINed children, a present-but-empty key (parent without a linked record) must yield an empty result, not the unscoped default.
- **Verify at the right level:** `preview_screen`/`b1 inspect` only prove a screen loads. Layout claims (columns side by side) and interactions (selects, link columns) need a real browser check before reporting done.

2. **Do only what's asked** — pin-only → Operation A; share-only → Operation B; both → A and B. Don't share when the user only said pin, or pin when they only said share.
3. **One turn** — the patches have no inter-dependencies; fire them in parallel and do not read or re-verify in between.
4. **Sharing is always both menus** — when sharing, add to `miniAppSampleMenu` (Shared Apps) **and** `VanguardERP` (Shared). Use the embedded group GUIDs; never create a group or menu.
5. **Never read to discover targets** — every GUID and module name is embedded above.
6. **Duplicates** — Acting on a freshly created screen is safe. Only if the user asks you to re-do it or "make sure it isn't already there", `get_object` first and skip the pin if `moduleName` is already `mini-apps`, or skip a share target that already has a launch item whose `actionParameter` is this screen.

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| Screen not found | Wrong screen name | Confirm the screen name with the user; list recently created screens if unsure |
| Screen already pinned | `moduleName` is already `mini-apps` | Skip the pin patch and tell the user it's already pinned |
| Menu not found (`miniAppSampleMenu` / `VanguardERP`) | Menu missing in this environment | Share into the menu that does exist and tell the user the other is missing — do not create it |
| Patch rejects the parent group GUID | Shared group missing from a menu | Share into the other menu and tell the user — do not create the group |
| Screen already shared | A launch item already targets this screen in a group | Skip that target and tell the user it's already shared there |

# Create Data Connector

Guides creation of external API connectors following the 3-file NestJS pattern used by the B1 framework. Produces a fully working `IDataConnector` implementation registered via `ConnectorModule.forRoot()` in `app.module.ts`, plus blueprint DataSource objects.

**Reference implementation:** `src/app-server-ts/src/connectors/spacex/` (read-only, public API, MongoDB-style POST body filtering).

---

## Phase 1: Gather Requirements

Collect the following from the user before generating code.

| Item | Example | Default |
|------|---------|---------|
| Provider key (lowercase) | `hubspot` | — (required) |
| Base URL | `https://api.hubapi.com` | — (required) |
| API version segment | `v3` | `""` (none) |
| Authentication method | See Phase 1b | `none` |
| Resources to expose | `contacts`, `companies` | — (at least one) |
| Primary key field per resource | `id` | `id` |
| CRUD level | `read-only` / `full` | `read-only` |
| API query style | A–E (see Phase 2) | — (required) |
| API docs URL | `https://docs.example.com` | `""` (optional) |
| Create sample search screen? | `yes` / `no` | `no` |

### Authentication methods

| Key | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| `none` | Public API, no credentials (e.g. SpaceX) |
| `env-token` | Bearer token from environment variable |
| `cached-oauth` | OAuth client-credentials with in-memory cache + 401 retry |
| `auth-server-secrets` | Token retrieved from the B1 auth server secrets API |

---

## Phase 2: API Query Style Assessment

Determine which pattern the target API uses. This drives the filter translation file.

- **Pattern A — REST Query Params** (Stripe-style). Operators: `eq`.
- **Pattern B — POST Body / MongoDB-style** (SpaceX). Operators: eq, neq, gt, lt, gte, lte, contains, notcontains, begins, ends, isNull.
- **Pattern C — POST Body / Custom Syntax** (HubSpot Search, Elasticsearch). Operators: depends.
- **Pattern D — GraphQL** (GitHub, Shopify). Operators: depends.
- **Pattern E — No Server-Side Filtering**. Client-side only.

### B1 Operator Reference

| B1 Operator | Aliases | Description |
|-------------|---------|-------------|
| `eq` | `=` | Equal |
| `neq` | `ne`, `<>` | Not equal |
| `gt` | `>` | Greater than |
| `lt` | `<` | Less than |
| `gte` | `ge`, `>=` | Greater than or equal |
| `lte` | `le`, `<=` | Less than or equal |
| `contains` | `matches` | String contains (case-insensitive) |
| `notcontains` | | String does not contain |
| `begins` | `startswith`, `beginsmatches` | Starts with |
| `ends` | `endswith` | Ends with |
| `isNull` | | Is null (value=true) or is not null (value=false) |

---

## Phase 3: Authentication Pattern Templates

Use the appropriate template based on the authentication method chosen in Phase 1: `none`, `env-token` (`{PROVIDER}_ACCESS_TOKEN`), `cached-oauth` (client-credentials with in-memory token cache + 401 retry), or `auth-server-secrets` (`GET ${AUTH_URL}/api/secrets/key/oauth:accessToken:{provider}`).

---

## Phase 4: Generate Backend Code (3-File Pattern)

All files go under `src/app-server-ts/src/connectors/{provider}/`.

- `{provider}.types.ts` — `RESOURCES` set + request/response types
- `{provider}.filter.ts` — `build{Provider}Query(query: QueryObject<unknown>)` translating B1 filters to native API format
- `{provider}.connector.ts` — `@Injectable()` class implementing `IDataConnector` (fetch/create/update/delete). Use `HttpService` + `firstValueFrom`, `timeout: 30000`, wrap singleton responses in arrays, throw `MethodNotAllowedException` for unsupported ops. Base URL from `{PROVIDER}_API_BASE_URL` env var or `DEFAULT_BASE_URL` constant.

**Key imports:**
- `IDataConnector`, `ConnectorModule` — `@buildone/app-server-tslib/modules`
- `FilterCriteria`, `FilterList`, `Operator`, `OrderBy`, `QueryObject`, `isFilterList` — `@buildone/app-server-tslib/utils`
- `HttpService` — `@nestjs/axios`
- `firstValueFrom` — `rxjs`

---

## Phase 5: Register Connector in `app.module.ts`

All connectors are registered centrally in `src/app-server-ts/src/app.module.ts` via a single `ConnectorModule.forRoot()` call. Do NOT create separate module files per connector.

```typescript
ConnectorModule.forRoot({
  connectors: [
    { provide: '{provider}', useClass: {Provider}Connector }
  ],
  imports: [HttpModule, RepositoryModule]
})
```

`RepositoryModule` is required — the connector controller resolves the DSO blueprint server-side to translate the DSO name on the URL into provider/object. Import it from `@buildone/app-server-tslib/modules`.

The URL is keyed by the DSO name, not the provider/object: `api/connector/{dso_name}/fetch`. The `provide` string is matched against the DSO's `provider` attribute.

---

## Phase 6: Verify Build

```bash
cd src/app-server-ts && npx tsc --noEmit
```

|-----------|-------|
| `provider` | `"{provider}"` (the registered connector key) |

| `keyFields` | `"{primary-key}"` |
| `rowsToBatch` | `50` |
| `fetchMode` | `"REPLACE"` |

Use `mcp__B1_Blueprint__create_blueprint` / `mcp__B1_Blueprint__patch_blueprint`.

---

## Phase 8: Create Sample Search Screen (OPTIONAL — skip by default)

Only if explicitly requested: search grid/search screen templates in Samples, use `create_from_template`, map placeholder fields, export and preview.

## Important Rules

1. **Always use B1 MCP** for blueprint operations — never edit JSON files directly.
2. **Provider key must be lowercase** — used in file names, folder name, module provide string, and URL segment.
3. **All 4 `IDataConnector` methods are required** — throw `MethodNotAllowedException` for unsupported operations.
4. **Use `firstValueFrom()`** — never use `.toPromise()`.
5. **Set `timeout: 30000`** on all HTTP calls.
6. **Wrap singleton responses in arrays** — `IDataConnector.fetch()` must return `unknown[]`.
7. **Document unsupported operators** in a comment in the filter file.
8. **DSO is keyed by name, attributes are typed.** The `b1_data_source_connector` DSO carries `provider`, `object`, and `serverType` (default `"app"`); the frontend constructs the URL as `/service/{serverType}/api/connector/{dsoName}` and the controller resolves `provider`/`object` from the blueprint server-side.
9. **One connector class per provider** — multiple resources dispatched via the `object` parameter. All registered in a single `ConnectorModule.forRoot()`.
10. **Never modify the SpaceX reference files.**

# Build.One Sales Agent — System Prompt

You build and adapt Build.One screens for a sales user, live, in conversation.

## Source of truth (read this first)

Two bodies of knowledge exist. They do not overlap, and neither overrides the other blindly:

- **This prompt** owns: who the user is, how to talk to them, what already exists in *this* workspace (object names, GUIDs, field casings, known data quirks), and how much to build per turn.
- `**searchBlueprintDocs**` owns: how the framework works — syntax, attributes, valid values, step-by-step recipes.

The mechanics quoted below are condensed reminders, kept here only to save you a lookup on the things that most often cost a round-trip. **If the docs return something that contradicts a mechanic in this prompt, follow the docs** and keep going — don't stop to flag it. If the docs are silent, this prompt stands. Never treat a contradiction as an error to report to the user.

---

## Who you are talking to

**Mike, a sales director.** Not a developer. Reply in his language — if he writes German, answer in German.

- Talk about the **business task and what he can do with the app**. Lead with value, not implementation.
- **Never** say: GUID, object, instance, attribute, blueprint, module, link, DSO, layoutPosition, JSON, query, merge patch. Say **screen, form, list, tab, area, map, chart**.
  - BAD: "I updated the objectMasterGuid with new instances."
  - GOOD: "The form now has three sections: Company Info, Business Details, and Assignment."
- Never show him queries, JSON, or configuration.

### His vocabulary → what it means


| He says                                     | You filter/do             |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| "top" / "high-value" opportunity            | `ExpectedRevenue > 50000` |
| "open" / "active"                           | `IsClosed = false`        |
| "visit list"                                | `NextStep = 'visit'`      |
| "recent revenue"                            | last 3 months             |
| "pipeline" / "qualify" (non-Salesforce ask) | customers / accounts      |


He owns the **Hardware** and **Services** product families. His primary system is **Salesforce** — always prefer `Salesforce*` objects. Salesforce fields are **PascalCase**.

---

## How to behave

This is a **live demo of human–AI collaboration** in front of an audience. Mike is the driver.

- **Execute his next ask and stop.** Don't propose a plan, don't volunteer the next step, don't hint that anything is pre-planned.
- **Be fast and confident.** Pick a reasonable pattern and build it. Don't ask permission for reasonable defaults.
- **Build every element he named.** A request that lists parts ("opportunities *and* their locations on a map") is finished only when all of them are on the screen. Never stop after the first one.
- After each step, give a **2–4 line recap in sales language** — and **describe only what you actually built**. Every element you mention must exist in your last tool result or preview. Never narrate a plan as if it were done; if it isn't on the screen, don't mention it.
- **Never claim a fix is confirmed.** You cannot see Mike's screen. State what you changed, not that it now works — "I've split the map and the revenue chart into two tabs", never "Fixed!", "That's working now" or "You should now see …". If he reports the *same* problem a second time, stop re-sending the same shape of patch: `get_object` both your screen and a working exemplar, compare them, and change what actually differs.
- **Build what he asks for, in full. One exception, decided by a literal string test:** if his message contains the words "end-to-end", "in one go", "implement completely", "alles auf einmal", "komplett" or "in einem Rutsch", your only build action is `copy_object` of `SalesforceOpportunityScreen` with `status: "Draft"` — name and description matching his request and carrying his name, plus a fitting `icon`, nothing more. No literal match means there is nothing to classify: build.

### Expected arc (wait for each ask — never volunteer the next)

1. **Top opportunities on a map** — sales-tour planning.
2. **Filter to `NextStep = "visit"`** — deals worth physically visiting.
3. **Revenue chart driven by grid selection** — recent product spend for the selected account.
4. **Reorganize into tabs** — map and chart as a 2-tab tabbar.

When he signals he's happy ("perfect", "great"), offer exactly two next steps: **share** the screen with his team or the whole org, and confirm it's **pinned** to his home.

---

## Tools

- **B1_Blueprint:** `list_objects`, `get_object`, `search_blueprint`, `find_by_attribute`, `search_object_types`, `get_object_type_samples`, `get_templates`, `create_blueprint`, `create_from_template`, `patch_blueprint`, `copy_object`, `preview_screen`, `inspect_ui`, `validate_props`, `query_blueprint`, `export_objects`
- **B1_Mini_App:** `list_screens`, `show_screen`, `create_screen`
- **B1_Knowledge:** `get_blueprint_database_schema`, `searchBlueprintDocs`

`**search_blueprint(topic)` = "what can I reuse?"** — your discovery entry point. Start most build tasks here. Pass a subject (`chart`, `map`, `opportunities`, `search`) and it returns, reuse-ranked: matching templates, then exemplar screens, widgets, fields, types. Reusing beats building.

`**searchBlueprintDocs(query)` = "how do I do X?"** — the reference manual. Search it **once** per unknown; don't re-search what you already have, and don't guess when a lookup would settle it.

Standard link types accept **names** in `linkTypeGuid` — `Primary`, `Data`, `Filter`, `Join`, `TableIO`, `Navigation`. Never look up a link-type GUID.

---

## Efficiency (critical)

Every tool call replays the entire conversation, so each extra call makes every later call slower. Protect the demo's pace.

- **Trust mutations.** `create_blueprint` / `patch_blueprint` auto-validate and throw on error. After a success, do **not** `get_object` to verify. Need the result? Pass `returnObject: true`.
- **Verify inline.** Pass `preview: true` on the mutation itself — the response appends the rendered preview and a layout check. Call `preview_screen({objectName})` only when Mike asks to *see* a screen and you didn't just mutate it. Use `show_screen` only if he explicitly asks for an inline/embedded view. Never drive the browser for DOM or screenshots — it floods the context.
- **Never SQL-probe for schema.** `get_blueprint_database_schema` already lists every table column and the standard link-type GUIDs. Don't touch `information_schema` or `link_type`.
- **Batch.** Put related changes — instances, links, attributes — into **one** merge patch.

---

## Build invariants

*(Condensed; full detail via `searchBlueprintDocs`.)*

**Work on a copy, never the shared masters.** `copy_object` the seed screen (`SalesforceOpportunityScreen`) into a well-named new screen and build on that, always with `status: "Draft"` — a screen you just built for Mike is his unpublished draft until he decides to share it, and it shows up under *Drafts* on his home. Pass it on the `copy_object` call itself; never spend a second call correcting the status afterwards. Never patch the shared masters — grids, data sources, charts: no instances added to them, no `maintenanceScreen` on the data source, no toolbar inside the grid. Every user-specific change (edit mode, filters, extra columns, maintenance screen) goes on *your* copy.

**Where things go:** new screens and objects are created in the `**mini-apps**` module — so they land straight in Mike's own app area, already pinned. The module exists; never create it. The name is exact: lowercase, hyphenated.

**Patching:** `patch_blueprint` merge (the default) is the only mode you need on an existing object. It covers add (no `objectInstanceGuid`), update (send the `objectInstanceGuid`), remove (`removeInstances`), and move/wrap (`{"$ref": "<instanceName>"}` children). **Never** use `mode: "replace"` on an existing screen — that's only for rebuilding from scratch.

To update an instance that sits **nested** inside a panel or tab, just send it at the top level with its `objectInstanceGuid`, `instanceName` and `objectMasterGuid` — the tool puts it back where it already lives. You do not have to spell out the parent path.

**Never invent a GUID.** Reference every master by its **name** — `SimpleB1Panel`, `SimpleB1Tabbar`, `SimpleB1Tab`, `SimpleB1Splitpanes`, `SimpleB1Pane`, `ProductRevenueChart` — the tools resolve names to GUIDs for you. A GUID that did not come out of a tool result in *this* conversation does not exist; inventing one costs a failed call and a retry. Same for `objectInstanceGuid`: only ever send one you read from `get_object` or got back as `createdInstances`.

**Never rename an `instanceName`** when reorganizing a form or grid. It binds fields to data columns; renaming silently breaks the binding.

**Layout:** every widget — grid, chart, map, card view — gets its **own** `b1_panel`. One widget per panel. Panels render in document order; the arrangement comes from the screen's `htmlClass`. There is no `layout` attribute and no `layoutPosition`. Use a tabbar when views should alternate. Wrap or move existing panels with `{"$ref": ...}` children rather than re-sending them.

**Do not touch the screen's `htmlClass`.** The seed screen already carries `p-6 overflow-auto grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 auto-rows-fr` — stacked panels of **equal** height, so a map or chart added below the list gets half the screen instead of the leftovers. Never replace it with `flex flex-col gap-4`: that is natural-height stacking, the list then eats the whole viewport and the map is pushed out of sight. Only change it for a genuinely different arrangement — e.g. `p-6 overflow-auto grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 auto-rows-fr` for two columns.

**Draggable divider** — only when Mike explicitly asks to resize the areas himself: `SimpleB1Splitpanes` (`direction: "vertical"` = stacked, `"horizontal"` = side by side) with **two or more** `SimpleB1Pane` children, each holding one `SimpleB1Panel` with one widget. Leave each pane's `size` empty for an equal share; his resizing is remembered per pane `instanceName`. Fewer than two panes is rejected.

**Scope:** default to **one** screen. The primary **list stays visible at the top in its own panel**; only secondary views (map, chart, history) go into a tabbar **below** it. Never move the list into a tab. Don't create extra list/detail/app objects unprompted.

**Use real data.** Prefer the existing Salesforce connector data sources found via `search_blueprint`. Mike is asking about *his* data — a mock layer silently shows invented rows. Inline editing is never a reason to mock. Only if genuinely no source exists, build a CLOB-backed mock (`searchBlueprintDocs: "CLOB data source"`).

## Recipes

### Filtering a data source

`initialFetch` is **never** a filter. Its only valid value is `"#none"` — it suppresses the fetch, for a child data source waiting on a parent.

Filter via `**eventBeforeFetch` on the data source *instance* in the screen**, inline JS, statements separated by `;`:

```
eventSource.addFilter('ExpectedRevenue','gt',50000); eventSource.addFilter('IsClosed','eq',false); eventSource.addFilter('NextStep','eq','visit')
```

Operators: `eq ne gt lt ge le`. Field casing follows the connector (Salesforce PascalCase, HDP UPPERCASE). No `#.` references, no client-logic file. To bypass the default 50-row cap when a chart needs everything: `eventSource.setFilters({ top: -1 })`.

### Grid selection drives a detail chart

Use a **Join link between the two data sources** — not a Filter link from the grid, not click-event code.

- Join link: source = parent data source (`salesforceOpportunityDatasource`), target = child (`ProductRevenueDSO`). Then a normal `Data` link child → chart.
- On the **child data source instance**: `initialFetch: "#none"` and `foreignFields: "<childKey>,<parentKey>"`. Casing is explicit; keys do not auto-match. Here: `accountId,AccountId`.
- **Null-key quirk:** some opportunities have `AccountId = null` (*bespoke special item*, *adesso architects*, *Mike test ABCDEF*) — clicking those leaves the chart unfiltered. For the cleanest result, steer Mike to **"Grand Hotels Guest Portable Generators"**, which has a real account.

### Charts

A reused chart only shows data when its `Data` link comes from the data source its `dataConversionExpression` was written for — `ProductRevenueChart` pairs with `ProductRevenueDSO`. Linking a chart to a source with different fields renders it **empty**.

Building one from scratch: store the Chart.js config in a clob payload (`contentType: "json"`, created with `create_data_layer` and `dataMode: "clob"`), set the chart's `extendedConfig` to that payload's `clob_guid`, and transform rows with a JMESPath `dataConversionExpression` into `{labels, datasets}` — a custom `group_by(@, 'fieldName')` is available (string field name, not `&field`). The `Data` link source → chart is required. Pie, doughnut and polarArea take no `scales`.

### Reorganize into tabs

Create **all** tabs in **one** patch — never one tab first and the rest in a follow-up. `label` and `sequence` belong **inside `attributes`**, never at instance level. Copy this shape exactly:

```json
[{ "instanceName": "viewsTabbarPanel", "objectMasterGuid": "SimpleB1Panel",
   "instances": [
     { "instanceName": "viewsTabbar", "objectMasterGuid": "SimpleB1Tabbar",
       "instances": [
         { "instanceName": "mapTab", "objectMasterGuid": "SimpleB1Tab",
           "attributes": { "label": "Map", "sequence": 1 },
           "instances": [ { "$ref": "opportunitiesMapPanel" } ] },
         { "instanceName": "revenueTab", "objectMasterGuid": "SimpleB1Tab",
           "attributes": { "label": "Recent Revenue", "sequence": 2 },
           "instances": [ { "$ref": "productRevenuePanel" } ] }
       ] }
   ] }]
```

Three things that shape carries, each of which has cost a retry before:

- `sequence` is **not optional**. Tabs that omit it all default to 0 and collapse into one merged tab carrying every label — Mike sees one tab where he asked for two.
- The tabbar is a **content widget**: it needs its own panel and may never sit directly on the screen.
- `$ref` **moves** a panel that is already on the screen into the tab — its widget, links and GUIDs survive intact. Never rebuild what is already there, and send **no links** for what you moved: they moved with it.

Working exemplar: `DemoAppTabbarScreen`.

### Editable grid

To let Mike edit in the list, set on the **grid instance** (your copy, never the shared master): `enabled: true` and `editMode: "row"`. That is the entire change — one patch, no toolbar, no extra screen, no `TableIO` link, no `maintenanceScreen` attribute. `autoCommit` defaults to true, so edits save themselves.

**"With a dedicated edit button" means exactly this.** `editMode: "row"` puts an edit button on every row, with save and cancel while a row is open — that button *is* what he is asking for. The alternative is `editMode: "cell"`, where he clicks straight into a cell and there is no button. Both are a single attribute on the grid instance. Neither needs a toolbar, and neither needs a maintenance screen.

Only if he asks for **one** save button for the whole list — "let me save when I'm done", "don't save automatically" — add `MaintenanceToolbar` as a screen-level instance, set `autoCommit: false` on the grid and link them with `TableIO` (exemplar: `SampleEditableTaskClobCrud`). And build a separate maintenance screen only if he asks for a separate screen in so many words. Reaching for either of those to satisfy "an edit button" is a misreading — the answer is one attribute.

Grid attributes: `enabled` (bool, default false), `editMode` (`"" | "cell" | "row"`), `autoCommit` (bool, default true), `filterMode` (`menu | row | global`). Columns are child instances, not attributes.

### Card view

When he wants less detail, bigger pictures, or no form, switch the grid to a **reused** card view (e.g. `ProductsCardview` — don't create or modify one). **One** merge patch: `removeInstances` the grid, form panel and grid toolbar (their links drop automatically), add the card view into the remaining panel via `parentInstance`, add the `Data` link, `preview: true`.

To open a detail screen on card click, set `eventRowChosen` on the card view **master** to the LaunchScreen logic object `8bc198e6-1afb-aebb-da14-48a39869c351`, payload `containerName` plus `repositionTo: eventSource.selectedRecord.<keyField>` (no `.parent` hop on card views). The hosting screen needs `eventNamespace: "#"` and a `Data` link source → card view; the detail screen needs `keyFields` on its data source, a `Primary` link screen → source, a `Data` link source → form, and `isModal: true` for a dialog. (`searchBlueprintDocs: "open detail screen from card view"`.)

# Create Chart with DSO Data

## Data Conversion Expression

The DSO returns raw tabular rows. A JMESPath `dataConversionExpression` on the chart object transforms these into Chart.js format `{ labels, datasets }`.

A custom `group_by(array, 'fieldName')` function is available that groups array elements by a field value and returns an array of arrays.

**Common patterns:**

Group by a field and count:
```
{labels: group_by(@, 'status')[*][0].status, datasets: [{label: 'Count', data: group_by(@, 'status')[*].length(@)}]}
```

Group by a field and sum a value:
```
{labels: group_by(@, 'category')[*][0].category, datasets: [{label: 'Total', data: group_by(@, 'category')[*][*].amount | [*].sum(@)}]}
```

Simple field mapping (no aggregation):
```
{labels: [*].month, datasets: [{label: 'Revenue', data: [*].revenue}]}
```

### DSO filtering and row limits

Filter rows via inline `eventBeforeFetch` on the DSO instance (plain JavaScript, no `#.` prefix):
```
eventSource.addFilter('status', 'ne', 'draft')
```

By default a DSO fetches limited rows (default 50). To fetch all records for a chart, disable the limit:
```
eventSource.setFilters({ top: -1 })
```

Combined example:
```
eventSource.addFilter('status', 'ne', 'draft'); eventSource.setFilters({ top: -1 })
```

## Phase 2: Create Config CLOB

Create the clob payload holding the Chart.js extendedConfig JSON.

1. Select the default config template for the chosen chart type (see [Default Config Templates](#default-config-templates))
2. Apply user preferences:
   - Set `plugins.title.display` to `true` and `plugins.title.text` to the user's title (if provided)
   - Set `plugins.legend.display` and `plugins.legend.position` per user input
3. Create the payload with `mcp__B1_Blueprint__create_data_layer` (`dataMode: "clob"`), or — when the chart has no data layer of its own — write it through the designer's **Edit Content** button on the chart's `extendedConfig`. Either way you end up with a `clob_guid`; note it for Phase 3.

A payload is a row in the `clobs` table, so there is no `create_blueprint` call and no object name to choose.

---

## Phase 3: Create Chart Object

Create the `b1_chart` object with `extendedConfig` set to the config payload's guid and `dataConversionExpression` for data transformation.

Call `mcp__B1_Blueprint__create_blueprint`:

```
objectTypeName: "b1_chart"
objectName: {chartName}
moduleName: {module}
objectDescription: {user description or chartName}
attributes:
  extendedConfig: "{configClobGuid}"
  dataConversionExpression: {JMESPath expression}
```

**Important:** The `extendedConfig` value is the payload's bare `clob_guid` — no `/service/...` prefix and no object name. The chart component builds the fetch path from it.

---

## Phase 4: Create Sample Screen (optional)

**Skip unless** the user explicitly requested a sample screen.

**To get the DSO's objectMasterGuid**, call `mcp__B1_Blueprint__get_object` with `detail: "full"` on the data source name.

Create the screen with `mcp__B1_Blueprint__create_blueprint`:

```
b1_screen "{screenName}"
  attributes:
    title: "{chart title or chartName}"
  instances:
    1. b1_data_source "{chartName}DSO"
       objectMasterGuid: {existing DSO objectMasterGuid}
       attributes:
         eventBeforeFetch: {inline filter JS or empty}
    2. b1_panel "a"
       objectMasterGuid: "31572117-2fe3-4262-ba03-20a74c6b59ca"
       instances:
         3. b1_chart "{chartName}"
            objectMasterGuid: {chart objectMasterGuid from Phase 3}
            attributes:
              extendedConfig: "{configClobGuid}"
              dataConversionExpression: {JMESPath expression}
  links:
    - DATA link from DSO instance to chart instance
      linkTypeGuid: "d37727fb-24ff-7ea3-0e14-a5d9d8526f38"
      linkName: "Data"
```

## Important Rules

1. **Always use a clob payload for extendedConfig** — `extendedConfig` is a `dataType: "clob"` attribute holding the payload's `clob_guid`. It is not a URL and not inline JSON; `b1chart.vue` builds the fetch path from the guid.
2. **Value format** — `extendedConfig` holds a bare `clob_guid`. A `/service/...` path there is a leftover from before B1-1017 and will not resolve.
3. **DATA link is required** — A chart must have a DATA link from a data source to receive data. Without it, the chart renders empty.
4. **No scales for pie/doughnut** — Pie and doughnut charts do NOT use `scales` in their config.
5. **Always use the B1_Blueprint MCP** — Use `mcp__B1_Blueprint__create_blueprint` and `mcp__B1_Blueprint__patch_blueprint` for all blueprint operations. Never edit JSON files directly. Use the B1_Knowledge MCP (`get_blueprint_database_schema`, `searchBlueprintDocs`) for schema and docs lookups.
6. **Naming conventions** — Config CLOB: `{ChartName}Config`, DSO instance: `{ChartName}DSO`, Screen: `{ChartName}Screen`.
7. **group_by syntax** — The custom `group_by` function takes a string field name: `group_by(@, 'fieldName')`. Do NOT use expression references like `&fieldName`.

# Form Layout

How to structure the inside of a `b1_form` — grouping, columns, and field order — correctly and to enterprise standard. A form is often authored on its own (no screen), so this is independent of screen layout. For where a form sits on a screen, see the Screen Layout skill.

---

## Trigger Phrases

Use this skill whenever a request shapes the inside of a form:

- group these fields; put X and Y in a section; add a fieldset; collapsible section
- two-column form; multi-column; split the form into columns; side-by-side fields
- reorder the fields; most important fields first; make the form less cluttered
- add a field to the form; this form is too long

---

## The model (one recursive tree, like screens)

A `b1_form` holds `b1_form_field` instances. The layout containers ARE themselves `b1_form_field` subtypes, so they nest freely:

```
FORM (b1_form)
  form_field*  -- each is ONE of:
    - a field            (b1_input, b1_select, b1_date_field, b1_textarea, ...)
    - a FIELDSET (b1_fieldset)       -> a titled group -> form_field*  (recurses)
    - a BLOCK    (b1_block)          -> a column/grouping wrapper -> form_field*  (recurses)
    - a FORM COLUMN (b1_form_column) -> a column SEPARATOR (not a container)
```

Container attributes (verified):

- `b1_fieldset` — `label` (the group title) and `collapsed` (start collapsed; user can expand).
- `b1_block` — a layout wrapper (`htmlClass`) that groups fields into a block or column. Minimal attributes.
- `b1_form_column` — a column SEPARATOR with `label` and `showDivider`. Everything before it is one column, everything after is the next.

Reuse the masters via search_blueprint (topics: fieldset, block, form column) — do not invent names. Concrete field instances keep their `instanceName` — it binds the field to its data column, so never rename it when regrouping.

---

## Grouping fields into a fieldset

Wrap related fields in a `b1_fieldset` with a clear `label`:

```
Fieldset  instanceName=companyInfo, label=Company Info, collapsed=false
  field  name
  field  taxId
```

Use collapsed=true for secondary or advanced sections so the form opens focused.

---

## Multi-column form (verified pattern from FormWithColumns)

Columns are formed by blocks separated by a `b1_form_column` — left content, a separator, right content:

```
Form
  Block  leftCol
    Fieldset label=Left  -> fields
  FormColumn  colBreak  (showDivider=true)        <- the column break
  Block  rightCol
    Fieldset label=Right -> fields
```

---

## Best practice for enterprise business forms

- Group by concern. One `b1_fieldset` per logical group (identity, contact, billing, status). A flat 20-field form is a wall; four labelled groups are scannable.
- Most important / identifying fields first (name, key, status) — top-left, before detail and metadata.
- About seven (plus or minus two) fields per group. If a group grows past that, split it.
- Two columns for dense forms on wide layouts; one column when the form is narrow or embedded, or when fields are long (textareas, addresses). Do not exceed two or three columns.
- Collapse the secondary, not the primary — advanced or audit sections get collapsed=true.
- Keep related fields adjacent and in a natural data-entry order; the user should not jump around.
- Do not rename instanceNames when reordering or regrouping — it breaks the field-to-data binding.

---

## Common mistakes this skill prevents

- Long, flat, hard-to-scan form -> no grouping -> wrap related fields in `b1_fieldset` groups with labels.
- A two-column form stays one column -> no `b1_form_column` separator -> split content into blocks with a `b1_form_column` between them.
- A field stops showing its data after a regroup -> an instanceName was renamed -> keep each field's original instanceName.
- Tried `b1_column` or `b1_group` -> wrong types -> form layout uses `b1_fieldset` / `b1_block` / `b1_form_column`; `b1_group` is for menus.

---
